measurement_scope: relational write surface (secondary index, unique constraint, foreign key, SQL INSERT/UPDATE via C API, 2-document SQL transaction), 1 and 8 writers, AFTER staging the opts.transaction_resolution commit path (TxnManager.resolveIntentsWithExtraBatchStaged / DBCore.resolveTransactionIntentsWithExtraBatchStaged): the apply lock and capi writer lane now release before this commit waits for durability, mirroring the primary write path (lite-single-commit-write-path.md section 3.2).
known_limitations: This fix removes the apply-lock-held-across-fsync defect on the transaction-resolution path (every SQL write through a table with a unique/FK constraint, and every explicit multi-document transaction). It does NOT reduce the number of distinct native commits a single writer pays for a coordinated-constraint or multi-statement write: durable_commits_per_write for unique-constraint/foreign-key/transaction modes is essentially unchanged from the before baseline (~11-16 commits/write vs ~2 for a plain/secondary-index SQL write). Folding the two-phase intent protocol (begin/writeIntents) and whatever else contributes the remaining ~10 commits into the SAME native transaction as the final resolve is follow-up work (a WS3/WS4-sized effort), not completed in this change.
Per-site stage tags for relational/integrity/transaction-resolution commits were not added, so the breakdown by concern is still not available in this report (same limitation as the before baseline).
mean_primary_group_size still reads 0.000 for every relational mode for the same reason as the before baseline.
